Every cell must have at least two same-coloured neighbours, so each colour class, viewed as a graph on the grid, has minimum degree at least 2. Such a graph contains a cycle, and the shortest cycle in the grid graph is a 2×2 block of 4 cells. So every colour is used on at least 4 squares, which gives at most 64/4 = 16 colours.

This bound is achieved by splitting the board into sixteen 2×2 blocks and painting each block its own colour. Each square then has two same-coloured neighbours inside its block.

ANSWER: 16
